failures.title: Caller froze defective interpretation in the new proposal
failures.finding: Public Agent prompt deliverable B requires the same six criteria with IDENTICAL check text, domain, mode, authority and scope and forbids weakening/strengthening them. It also forces the same historical request. This applies historical preservation to new proposed artifacts, although PHASE explicitly authorizes correcting contract defects in new artifacts. The specialist consequently cannot resolve an overstrict interpretation under that delegated output constraint.
failures.action: Preserve immutable historical artifacts and verdict bindings, but explicitly permit new proposal request/criteria text to change where required by a source comparison. Require original source outcomes to survive; do not require old interpretation text to remain identical.

failures.title: Final required color criterion still adds dominance
failures.finding: The final candidate-plan retains 'The dominant colour treatment...' under requirement authority. Caller calls its additions 'none' and compares another blue palette against a green check with one blue pixel; neither tests the source's lack of dominance requirement. The final contract is called consistent and complete.
failures.counterexample: A primarily neutral asymmetrical completion mark with a clearly perceptible cool-blue rim or inset can use the required UI accent while another color dominates. A token single blue pixel is not the only alternative to dominant blue.
failures.action: Keep the required visible cool-blue relationship and remove mandatory dominance, or split dominance into an explicitly scoped expert choice. Compare a meaningful source-conforming alternative that differs on extent, not only hue or tone count.

failures.title: Caller converts transparent background into an opaque-foreground plate ban
failures.finding: Caller-review explicitly states a check on an opaque rounded plate fails and the source excludes it because the plate would be a background. The source requires a transparent background but does not prohibit an intentional opaque backing component within a subject surrounded by transparent negative space. The same caller describes plate choice as open in ready-meaning.
failures.counterexample: An asymmetrical blue-accented check on a small intentional rounded badge, with alpha-zero exterior and sufficient readability at 1x/3x, can satisfy all source outcomes. An opaque full-canvas matte is a different construction.
failures.action: Distinguish exterior transparency from intentional foreground components; retain the transparent-background outcome while leaving backing shape as scoped art direction unless the owner explicitly bans it.

secondary_notes.finding: Useful measured raster and source-view discussion is mixed with unsupported absolutes: the caller calls a 2px effective stroke the minimum surviving 1x, while its ready-meaning alternative allows a thin 1px check. No comparison proving such a minimum is retained. Expert recipe proposals should be stated as candidate judgments rather than guaranteed necessities.
secondary_notes.boundary: This is a reasoning-quality caution, not a changed numerical acceptance criterion. It does not invalidate the measured 16x16 fixture or establish a separate broad corpus defect.
